toegepas.voor: gee jy dieselfde dinge vir jou eie kinders aan
toegepas.na: gee jy dieselfde dinge aan jou eie kinders oor
toegepas.rede_vinder: Customs are passed on with 'oorgee aan'; 'vir iemand aangee' means handing over an object.
toegepas.fout: 'vir jou kinders aangee' is the hand-an-object construction, copied from English 'pass on', for customs handed down
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Aan jou kinders oorgee' is the natural Afrikaans for handing customs to the next generation; same people, same direction.

toegepas.rede_vinder: No list was given, only a number of languages, so 'lys' has no clear referent.
toegepas.fout: 'Daardie lang lys' refers to a list the text never gives, only a count of languages
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Al daardie tale' points clearly at what was just named, without changing the claim.

toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS: a comma separates the verb closing the relative clause from the main-clause verb that follows it.
toegepas.fout: two verbs from different clauses meet ('praat kan') with no comma, so the reader stumbles
toegepas.rede_keurder: The AWS comma between the relative clause's closing verb and the main verb makes the sentence readable on first pass.

toegepas.blok: Kultuur sê nie hoe jy moet leef nie
toegepas.voor: in 'n groot stad en 'n ander gesin
toegepas.na: in 'n groot stad, en 'n ander gesin
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: 'en' joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb, so a comma goes before it.
toegepas.fout: 'en' joins two clauses each with its own subject and verb ('Een gesin woon' / 'n ander gesin woon') without the AWS comma

toegepas.blok: Kultuur sê nie hoe jy moet leef nie
toegepas.voor: Dit sit ook in die gewone dinge
toegepas.na: Dit lê ook in die gewone dinge
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Iets lê in' is the usual idiom for where a quality is found.
toegepas.fout: 'Dit sit in' is a loose colloquial form for where a quality is found
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Dit lê ook in' is the fixed Afrikaans expression and keeps the meaning.

toegepas.rede_vinder: The standard adjective form is 'Kaaps-Maleis(e)', and a dish comes 'uit' a cuisine.
toegepas.fout: 'Kaapse Maleier-kookkuns' is a non-standard compound; the standard adjective is 'Kaaps-Maleise'
toegepas.rede_keurder: Standard form, and 'uit' versus 'van' still says the dish belongs to that cuisine, so nothing moves.

toegepas.voor: in baie huise oor die land gebak
toegepas.na: in baie huise regoor die land gebak
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Regoor die land' is the idiomatic phrase for 'across the country'.
toegepas.fout: 'oor die land' is a loose rendering of 'across the country'
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Regoor die land' is the fixed Afrikaans expression with the same meaning.

toegepas.na: eerder as by sommer enige dag
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Sommer enige dag' carries the intended 'just any day'; 'enige dag' alone reads oddly after 'bepaalde dag'.
toegepas.fout: 'eerder as by enige dag' reads oddly against 'bepaalde dag'; the intended contrast is 'just any day'
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Sommer enige dag' is the natural Afrikaans for that contrast and adds no information.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Daar sit' is colloquial for existence; 'daar is' is the natural form here.
toegepas.fout: 'sit daar dikwels 'n les' is a colloquial existential form that reads stiffly here
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Is daar dikwels' is the natural form and keeps the qualifier 'dikwels' intact.

laat_vaar.voor: en nog baie ander tale daarby
laat_vaar.na: en daarby nog baie ander tale
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Placing 'daarby' before the noun phrase reads more naturally.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Lateral reorder; 'en nog baie ander tale daarby' already reads naturally.

laat_vaar.blok: Kultuur sê nie hoe jy moet leef nie
laat_vaar.voor: Albei daardie gesinne behoort nog altyd
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Nog altyd' means 'all along'; the sense here is 'still', which is 'steeds', and 'daardie' is redundant after 'albei'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Nog altyd' already means 'still' in Afrikaans, and 'albei daardie gesinne' is natural; the swap is lateral.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Gesterf het' is gentler and more usual when speaking of a family's bereavement.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Waar iemand dood is' is plain, natural Afrikaans for a Grade 4 reader; 'gesterf het' is only different.

na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'n Kwart' dangles without saying a quarter of what.
na_skrywer.fout: in the glossary entry 'dikwels 'n kwart' dangles without saying a quarter of what
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: A real fault, but it rewords a glossary definition beyond spelling or grammar, so the writer must fix it for every lesson at once.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'Meer' on its own is unclear; 'meer as een' states the plural plainly.
na_skrywer.fout: in the glossary entry 'meer heet amagwinya' leaves 'meer' unclear (more than one vetkoek)
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: A real fault, but the fix rewords a shared glossary definition, which only the writer may change.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.rede: The study block says people in Durban 'gewoonlik' order a quarter, the glossary says 'dikwels'; the qualifiers differ and only the writer can say which is intended.
